analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers passes most of my quantitative filters — P/E 8.91, P/B ~1.19, zero debt, 20% ROE, and six consecutive profitable years — a rarity among recent IPOs. However, the 2025 equity jump from 67 Cr to 171 Cr reveals fresh IPO proceeds that have yet to earn their keep, so I remain cautious until deployment is proven.
key_strengths: Graham Number ~153 vs price 98.10 gives ~36% margin of safety
Debt-free balance sheet; finance cost has fallen to zero
Net profit CAGR 39% with 5/5 years of positive operating cash flow
key_risks: Recent IPO (2025) — no multi-year track record as a listed entity; promoter/seller knows more than buyer
77 Cr investing outflow in 2025 — IPO cash not yet productive, ROE will dilute
Small-cap IT services (100 Cr revenue) — vulnerable to client concentration and INR/wage cycles
red_flags: IPO premium pricing — fresh listing with unproven capital allocation of 64 Cr financing inflow
No meaningful dividend history disclosed — cash return to shareholders unproven
analysis.detailed_analysis: On the numbers alone, this security clears several of my defensive screens: P/E under 10, P/B comfortably below 1.5 (book value per share ~82.65 vs price 98.10), no borrowings, interest coverage effectively infinite, and earnings that have compounded from 5 Cr to 26 Cr over 2020–2025. The Graham Number calculation — sqrt(22.5 × 12.56 EPS × 82.65 BVPS) ≈ 153 — suggests intrinsic value roughly 55% above the current quote, an unusual finding for a recent listing. ROCE of 26.5% and operating CF positive in every year of the record further corroborate genuine earning power rather than accounting fiction.
